cases.label: skip
cases.note: crontab(5): jobs in the missing hour never run; jobs in the repeated hour run twice — but the second half of that sentence is a *daemon* behaviour, so a library that returns a set must still choose.

cases.label: next_valid
cases.note: Fire at the first valid wall time at or after the nominal one (croniter's default; APScheduler; most cloud schedulers).

cases.label: fire_at_gap_start
cases.note: Corpus policy: clamp a nonexistent nominal wall time to the transition instant at which valid post-gap time begins. This vector's 23:30 wall time never reaches that branch.

cases.label: fold_both
cases.note: Emit both instants of an ambiguous wall time (Vixie daemon behaviour for repeated hours, and cronsim's option).

expectation.note: All five declared policy profiles intentionally produce the same occurrence set because 23:30 is outside the 2026 St_Johns gap and fold. This is a control, not a gap-policy discriminator.

normative_evidence.note: Compiled IANA tzdb 2026a places the St_Johns transition at 2026-03-08T05:30:00Z, from UTC-03:30 to UTC-02:30; local time jumps from 01:59:59 to 03:00:00.

rationale: America/St_Johns combines a fractional UTC offset with a modern DST rule. In 2026 the spring transition skips local 02:00-02:59, but this daily 23:30 wall time is outside the anomaly. The vector is therefore a negative control: it verifies UTC-03:30/UTC-02:30 conversion across a DST-observing zone without invoking a gap or fold policy.
title: Half-hour standard offset with DST (America/St_Johns, -03:30)
